transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-30 14:00 PT | Duration 52m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM intro), Lena (EmberCore CTO), Aaron (PM), Tom (Data Eng), Priya (Security)

Summary: quick discovery to size pilot for rerank + embeddings. EmberCore runs omnichannel search, currently uses Chroma for vectors and a lightweight cross-encoder for rerank on CPU; wants sub-200ms p50 for interactive flows and p95 under 500ms for rerank path. They are evaluating hosted for speed to prod, dedicated for throughput predictability, private for compliance.

[00:00:10] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, joining with maya on the se side and sofia to say hi. how's every one doing?
[00:00:18] Lena: good, thanks. been a busy quarter. we are curious about how you folks would run our rerank path, and cost/throughput tradeoffs.
[00:00:28] Jordan: great, was hoping to understand current stack and SLOs. aaron, can you give a quick overview of the flow?
[00:00:35] Aaron: sure yeah. user query -> bi-encoder retrieval against chro-ma vector DB -> top100 -> dense rerank cross-encoder to get top5 -> downstream scoring. rerank today is on CPU and it's slow, p50 around 450ms sometimes up to 1.2s. want to bring that down esp on mobile where latency is visible.
[00:01:05] Maya: ok how big is the embed fanout? topK 100? and what's embed dim?
[00:01:12] Aaron: we store 1536-d embeddings from an off-the-shelf model. fanout 100 in default, some flows do 300 for recommendation. qps varies: 80 steady during day, bursts to 400 during campaigns.
[00:01:30] Tom: we also run nightly reindex, plus some batch canonicalization. most traffic is read heavy.

[00:02:10] Jordan: thanks. key constraints i hear: throughput (steady and burst), p95 for interactive rerank, and security/compliance. are there any hard requirements on data residency?
[00:02:20] Priya: we have EU customers, so need EU residency for certain corp data. also must use KMS for key management and we've got an upcoming audit so SOC2 type 2 evidence is required.
[00:02:34] Jordan: got it. we can provide SOC2 docs, and redwood private supports bring-your-own-kms/hsm and vpc peering. we'll include the security pack after the call.

[00:03:00] Maya: quick follow on technical: is the rerank model a cross-encoder that requires full input pair scoring? that usually determines whether you want dedicated GPUs for low tail-latency.
[00:03:10] Aaron: yeah cross-encoder, roughly BERT-size, 110M-300M parameters depending on variant. CPU is the current gating factor.

[00:03:40] Maya: ok so two main patterns we see: 1) keep embeddings retrieval in your VDB and call redwood for cross-encoder rerank — that's common for hosted/dedicated; 2) bring both embed generation + rerank to redwood if you want single-vendor hosting and to reduce network hops. Both have tradeoffs on cost and latency.

[00:04:20] Lena: network hops are a concern. we have vector DB in same cloud but separate project, currently running Chroma on k8s. what's the typical added latency for a network hop to redwood hosted?
[00:04:32] Maya: depends on region and model size, but for hosted API in same region p50 adds 10-30ms for embed calls; rerank cross-encoder on a dedicated GPU pool with warmed KV cache we often see p50 under 120ms and p95 around 250-400ms for mid-size cross encoders. hidden: numbers vary with batch size and kernel optimizations.

[00:05:10] Aaron: for us, if p95 is 250-400ms that would be acceptable for most UX flows. but we also have batch flows that need throughput for bulk re-ranking of 100k items.
[00:05:22] Jordan: for large batch jobs we recommend Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling and burst capacity; private can be configured for on-prem-like constraints but costs go up. can you say more abt the offline job size?
[00:05:35] Tom: nightly we re-rank ~120k rows and run batched callouts. we need throughput more than single-request latency here.

[00:06:05] Maya: i want to call out quantization/precision. for embeddings you can usually go 8-bit or lower without big recall loss, for cross-encoder rerank we usually test 8-bit and 4-bit quantization on dedicated to trade accuracy vs throughput. any accuracy guardrails?
[00:06:20] Aaron: we have a small eval set and human judges; quality drop must be <1.5% on nDCG.

[00:06:35] Lena: curious about model variants and version pinning, esp during rollouts. can redwood host pinned versions and do canary rollouts?
[00:06:43] Jordan: yes pinned model versions and rollout policies (canary, A/B) are supported in both Hosted and Dedicated. Private has similar controls but depends on customer infra for orchestration.

[00:07:10] Priya: on the security side, what about audit logs and RBAC? we need token-level logging and per-team role separation.
[00:07:20] Maya: redwood console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and audit logs. RBAC and SSO via SAML/SSO can be integrated; for private we support your existing IdP and can do SCIM provisioning. note: some of the field names in the auto-logs get munged in transcription but the data is there.

[00:07:55] Aaron: we also use Pinecone for some ephemeral indices; any opinion on hybrid approach? e.g. keep dense retrieval in our VDB and use Redwood for rerank only?
[00:08:05] Maya: that's the common hybrid model: VDB for recall, redwood rerank for high-quality ranking. fallback strategies are important — if the dedicated cluster is saturated we can fallback to a cheaper cross-encoder or a smaller model variant to preserve availability.

[00:08:40] Jordan: what about embedding dim reduction? you said 1536 dims, that impacts vector DB storage and fanout cost. do you have upstream control to change dims?
[00:08:50] Tom: not yet, model outputs 1536 now. we could retrain smaller but cost to our team. prefer solution that works with 1536.

[00:09:10] Maya: ok we'll include cost estimates for 1536 dims and a lower-dim option like 768. often customers move to 768 or 1024 and run A/B to validate.

[00:09:40] Lena: can you run a quick back-of-envelope for our bursts? if we have 400 qps with 100 fanout and cross-encoder rerank per request, how do you size dedicated?
[00:09:52] Maya: rough math: if rerank cross-encoder costs ~30ms on a single GPU per pair (note: depends) and you do naive 100 scoring that's huge. but we do batching and prefix caching and a rerank pattern where retrieval is used to prune candidates — often rerank is only applied to topK 20 after a cheaper recall pass. for 400 qps with top20 rerank you'd want multiple GPUs with batching; a pilot cluster of 4 x A100 (or modern H100 variants) with shard routing and autoscale would be a starting point. dedicated gives consistent tail-latency.

[00:10:45] Aaron: what's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated? we need a ballpark.
[00:10:50] Jordan: hosted is usage-based; good for low-friction and initial rollouts. dedicated is committed capacity monthly which reduces per-token cost for sustained traffic and gives SLA. i'll send a pricing matrix but rough numbers: hosted per-token price for rerank will be higher at scale vs dedicated per-hour GPU amortized.

[00:11:20] Priya: about private deployment, we have a compliance requirement to keep some data in our VPC and to manage keys using our HSM. can redwood private support that?
[00:11:30] Maya: yes private is designed for that — private control plane with customer-managed networking and BYOK KMS/HSM integrations. we'll include the architectural diagram. note: private requires longer lead time for setup and extra ops involvement.

[00:12:05] Tom: integration with our Chroma — do you have connectors or should we proxy traffic?
[00:12:12] Maya: typical patterns: 1) call VDB from your app, get topK, call Redwood Hosted/Dedicated for rerank; 2) proxy retrieval through Redwood if you want server-side orchestration; 3) push embeddings to Redwood-managed vector cache for low-latency local rerank. We have scripts and examples for Pinecone/Chroma/Weaviate connectors.

[00:12:45] Aaron: any gotchas with KV cache? we saw docs mentioning k-v cache but our engs were confused.
[00:12:52] Maya: kv cache is redwood's internal key-value cache for decoder state; it's mostly for generation and autoregressive models. for rerank/cross-encoder less relevant but for embed generation and long context generation it's important. sometimes transcriptions show it as K-V cash or K V cache in the exported docs :)

[00:13:20] Jordan: i want to capture success criteria: what's required for you to sign a pilot?
[00:13:25] Lena: 1) proof that p95 rerank under 500ms for interactive flows, 2) cost estimate under our run-rate budget, 3) security docs and KMS option confirmed, 4) pilot SOW and timeline.

[00:13:42] Jordan: good, we can do that. propose next steps: we run a 2-week perf pilot using your sample queries and traces, set up a small dedicated cluster for rerank (or hosted if you want faster), and compare p50/p95 and embedding accuracy.

[00:14:10] Maya: can i ask about dataset sizes for the vdb? number of vectors?
[00:14:16] Tom: roughly 25 million vectors across all products, but indexing is sharded.

[00:14:30] Maya: okay scale matters for the VDB side. for the rerank pilot we only need the query distribution and a sample shard.

[00:15:02] Aaron: one more question — any customers running hybrid top-k + rerank at our scale? would like references.
[00:15:10] Jordan: yes a few retail and docs search customers — i'll include anonymized case studies and a contact for a reference call.

[00:15:30] Priya: about compliance evidence — do you provide SOC2 type2 report and penetration test summaries?
[00:15:38] Sofia: yes we'll share the security pack with SOC2, ISO attestation, pen test summaries, and our data processing addendum.

[00:16:00] Lena: instrumentation and observability — can we get per-request trace to our tracing backend?
[00:16:06] Maya: we have tracing hooks and can export traces to common backends (datadog, jaeger) and provide per-route metrics and token level breakdowns.

[00:16:30] Tom: curious about model lifecycle: if we push a new rerank model do you support a/b testing? can we roll back quickly?
[00:16:38] Maya: yes built-in rollouts, canary and automatic fallback to previous variant if metrics degrade; it's in console.

[00:17:05] Aaron: what about batch offline re-ranking at 120k rows per night — any recommended best practice?
[00:17:12] Maya: use a batch pipeline with quantized model for throughput, run on dedicated GPU spot pool or burst capacity. we often suggest converting rerank to candidate re-scoring in stages to reduce compute by pruning earlier.

[00:17:45] Jordan: do you have a timeline for pilot?
[00:17:48] Lena: want to kick off before the end of november ideally.

[00:17:55] Jordan: that aligns. we'll send SOW and pilot config by next week.

[00:18:10] [longer section of technical deep dive between Maya and Tom where they exchange specifics and sample commands]
[00:18:15] Maya: for bench harness we'll need: sample queries, expected topK, label set for nDCG, and tail latency traces. we'll provide a runner script that hits hosted endpoints and a dedicated config to spin up in our pilot env.
[00:18:35] Tom: ok i'll package logs. one thing — our infra team prefers to run performance runs from our corporate VPC to mimic network conditions. is that possible?
[00:18:42] Maya: yes for private you can run inside your VPC; for hosted we can provide agent-based runners or run from our infra in the same cloud region. we'll document the runner options.

[00:19:10] Aaron: on pricing and commitment — what does dedicated min look like?
[00:19:18] Jordan: depends on GPU type and region; a small dedicated cluster (3 nodes) with autoscale is common for pilot. i'll include a 3-node A100 and 4-node H100 scenario.

[00:19:45] Lena: what's typical SLA for dedicated?
[00:19:48] Jordan: we provide uptime SLA and latency SLOs for dedicated under a contractual commit. hosted has best-effort with degraded cost tiers, while private can be negotiated as part of enterprise contract.

[00:20:10] Priya: any data flow diagrams you can share? we need to show auditors.
[00:20:16] Sofia: yes we'll attach architecture doc and data flow diagrams in the email.

[00:20:40] Maya: quick note on fallback policies — if a large burst saturates dedicated, we can route to hosted or smaller model to avoid 503s; that's configurable per route.

[00:21:05] Tom: for our re-rank cross-encoder, do you support batching across requests to improve GPU utilization?
[00:21:12] Maya: yes continuous batching and kernel selection optimize throughput; we can tune target batch sizes and latency windows. also prefix caching is less relevant for rerank but we can do request coalescing when appropriate.

[00:21:45] Aaron: would love a quick excel with cost estimates for steady-state and burst.
[00:21:50] Jordan: yes will include cost matrix.

[00:22:10] [short pause, background noise, someone coughing; transcription shows slight garbling of a sentence]
[00:22:40] Maya: one more thing — on vector dims, if you stay at 1536 your vector DB storage and fanout costs scale linearly; we recommend consolidation or dimensionality reduction as a future step.

[00:23:05] Lena: ok we're comfortable with that. any immediate blockers?
[00:23:12] Priya: just need to review the security docs and confirm data residency.

[00:23:25] Jordan: action items: we'll send security pack, pricing, and bench harness. customer to provide traces and sample queries.

[00:23:40] Aaron: can we also get an estimated timeline for pilot setup?
[00:23:45] Maya: typical 2-3 weeks to stand up a pilot env if dedicated or private; hosted pilot can be same day. we'll propose dates in SOW.

[00:24:10] Lena: great thanks everyone.
[00:24:14] Jordan: thanks we'll follow up with docs and pricing.
[00:24:20] [meeting wrap, small talk about conferencing tool]

Notes on transcription artifacts: speaker labels sometimes off, 'k v cache' transcribed strangely as 'K-V cash', 'SAML' occasionally 'sammel', Redwood internal product name 'Optimize' was said but transcribed as 'polaris' by auto system.

End of transcript.
